method.processes: fresh process per backend per repeat
method.keys: mixed (hashed full-width), sequential (consecutive even) and clustered (runs of 1,024 consecutive even keys at scattered bases)
method.chart_statistic: 100 * (median Go operation time / median Rust operation time - 1)
method.distinct_churn: Unique keys selected by a coprime stride over the full insertion domain alternate with a disjoint key set. Every deletion must succeed with the expected value and every insertion must be fresh; checksums are independently computed by the Python harness.
method.distinct_operation_count: min(entries, queries) keys per round; rounds multiplied by floor(queries/min(entries, queries)). All recorded sizes execute 4194304 pairs.
method.replacement_validation: Serial replacements sum every bit of the previous value. Python independently computes the expected sum, accounting for duplicate queries; both drivers verify final values outside timing. Parallel replacement sums remain order-independent.
method.concurrent_contracts: Both concurrent maps omit len() and read payloads with plain loads validated by node versions. The Go Map ports the pinned Rust latched tree's protocol; the Rust implementation is unmodified.
method.string_keys: Byte-string cells write each mixed key as user: and 16 hex digits, with uint64 values: Rust String keys, Go gobbtree.Bytes ([]byte) keys, both made before the timed build. Rust's containers move the Strings in; Go's copy each key's bytes into their leaves, in buffers the collector doesn't scan, as a caller may change its slice afterwards. Rust replaces values with update and get_mut, Go with Insert; churn inserts back the String a removal returned, and Go the same Bytes. Go's Tree runs on the Map's tree as its single writer, taking no latches.

limitations: Desktop apps (the window server, a browser, an IDE) and other projects' processes kept the load average between 3.4 and 7.4 throughout the run. Small timing differences are inconclusive.

At 50M sequential keys both languages timed 1.4-2x slower than in the previous report, and two reruns in this session varied by as much again, both languages alike: those cells are the machine's state and inconclusive. The report keeps the matrix run's.

Most of the build cells Go now wins come from upstream's update to 8ef597b, whose sequential builds run slower than 1c72bd2's (262K Map 11.6 to 21.4 ns an entry, 4K 10.4 to 24.1); at 50M mixed keys both languages built 18-26% faster than in the previous report.

Four byte-string cells changed side against the previous report, each by 1-7%. The previous report's driver (ba66888), rerun beside this one at 262K in this session, timed every byte-string cell within 3% of it, so those flips are run-to-run variation.
CPU records include Go's builtin map and sync.Map at 4096, 262144 and 5000000 entries with mixed keys only.
Memory records cover Tree and Map.
